2609.25697.title: Interpretable AI plus Handheld, Portable Retinal Photographs: A Low-Cost Glaucoma Screening Solution for West Africa
2609.25697.paper_summary: Purpose: To develop and evaluate an interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) framework for glaucoma screening from low-cost portable, handheld retinal fundus photographs in a West African population and to compare its performance with clinical tabletop fundus imaging. Methods: We used data from a community-based study of 681 participants (1,362 eyes) in Nigeria, comprising 414 glaucoma, 478 glaucoma suspect, and 470 non-glaucoma eyes. Fundus photographs were acquired using the low-cost handheld, portable Volk Viva retinal camera and the Canon CR-2-AF tabletop camera. We fine-tuned component models separately to each device to perform vessel segmentation, cup and disc boundary segmentation, and feature extraction to detect optic nerve head features. A final classification model combined these components to classify scans as glaucoma, glaucoma suspect or non-glaucoma. Feature-weight analysis and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping were used for interpretation. Results: The models performed well on both Volk Viva and Canon CR-2-AF images: Vessel segmentation: 0.98 Dice Coefficient (DC) (Volk) and 0.94 DC (Canon); Cup and disc segmentation: 0.95 DC (Volk) and 0.96 DC (Canon); Optic nerve head feature detection: area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.83$\pm$0.03 (Volk) and 0.87$\pm$0.04 (Canon); Classification model: AUCs of 0.85$\pm$0.01 (Volk) and 0.93$\pm$0.01 (Canon). Reports for each image, present model decision confidence scores and decision-rationale visualizations to support clinical interpretation. Conclusions: Volk Viva results were reasonably comparable to Canon CR-2-AF in the component models and not far behind in classification. This shows that interpretable AI combined with low-cost, portable imaging may enhance community-level glaucoma screening, especially in settings with limited specialist access and resources.
2609.25697.paper_summary_zh: 目的：開發和評估一個可解釋的人工智慧（AI）框架，用於從低成本的便攜式手持視網膜眼底照片中進行青光眼篩查，針對西非地區的人群，並將其性能與臨床桌面眼底成像進行比較。<lb/>方法：我們使用了來自尼日利亞681名參與者（1,362隻眼睛）的社區基礎研究數據，包括414隻青光眼、478隻青光眼可疑眼和470隻非青光眼眼睛。<lb/>眼底照片是使用低成本的手持便攜式Volk Viva視網膜相機和Canon CR-2-AF桌面相機獲取的。<lb/>我們分別對每個設備的組件模型進行微調，以執行血管分割、杯盤邊界分割和特徵提取，以檢測視神經頭特徵。<lb/>最終分類模型將這些組件結合起來，將掃描結果分類為青光眼、青光眼可疑或非青光眼。<lb/>特徵權重分析和梯度加權類別激活映射被用於解釋。<lb/>結果：這些模型在Volk Viva和Canon CR-2-AF影像上表現良好：血管分割：0.98 Dice Coefficient (DC)（Volk）和0.94 DC（Canon）；杯盤分割：0.95 DC（Volk）和0.96 DC（Canon）；視神經頭特徵檢測：受試者工作特徵曲線下面積（AUCs）為0.83$\pm$0.03（Volk）和0.87$\pm$0.04（Canon）；分類模型：AUCs為0.85$\pm$0.01（Volk）和0.93$\pm$0.01（Canon）。<lb/>每張影像的報告中，呈現模型決策信心分數和決策理由可視化，以支持臨床解釋。<lb/>結論：Volk Viva的結果在組件模型中與Canon CR-2-AF相當可比，且在分類上也不遜色。<lb/>這表明，可解釋的AI結合低成本的便攜式成像可能會增強社區層級的青光眼篩查，特別是在專家訪問和資源有限的環境中。
